entities.summary: The Edsall-class destroyer escorts were destroyer escorts built primarily for ocean antisubmarine escort service during World War II. The lead ship, USS Edsall, was commissioned on 10 April 1943 at Orange, Texas. The class was also known as the FMR type from their Fairbanks-Morse reduction-geared diesel drive, with a type of engine used in the submarines of the time. The FMR's substitution for a diesel-electric power plant was the essential difference from the predecessor Cannon ("DET") class. This was the only World War II destroyer escort class in which all the ships originally ordered were completed as United States Navy destroyer escorts.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Edsall-class destroyer escorts played a crucial role in ocean antisubmarine escort service during World War II, contributing to the Allied victory. With all ships originally ordered completed as United States Navy destroyer escorts, they represented a significant shift from their predecessor Cannon class.
